messages:
olivia_chen: Hey team, first-day snag. I ran docker-compose and the web app (running on host) can't talk to Redis: `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6379`. Also Postgres in the container logged `could not bind IPv4 socket: Address already in use`. I'm on macOS and didn't change the compose file. Any onboarding tips?

matt_b: Welcome @olivia_chen! Likely you have host services (brew) using the same ports. Run `lsof -i :6379 -i :5432` or `brew services list` to check.

olivia_chen: Running `brew services list` shows redis started and postgresql started. Oops. I didn't expect that. Should I stop them?

sara_l: You have options: (A) stop the brew services while you develop: `brew services stop redis postgresql` (fast); (B) don't expose ports in compose and run the web inside compose so it uses service names (more parity); (C) remap ports in compose to host ports that don't conflict (e.g., 63790:6379, 54330:5432) and update your local .env.

matt_b: If your dev workflow uses host edit/reload, option C or stopping brew is easiest. If you want to preserve your host DB/Redis for other projects, remap ports and add a `.env.local` (gitignored) with `REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:63790` and `DATABASE_URL=postgres://redwood:pass@localhost:54330/redwood_dev`.

olivia_chen: I prefer host dev for fast reloads. I tried remapping ports but the app still fails to connect; `docker-compose ps` shows the ports mapped correctly.

sara_l: Two extra things to check: 1) Are you running the web outside compose? If so the host process needs to point at the remapped ports. 2) If your app previously used unix sockets (e.g., `postgresql:///redwood?host=/var/run/postgresql`), remapping won't help unless you switch to TCP.

olivia_chen: Good call — my local .env had DATABASE_URL using a socket path. I updated it to TCP and now Postgres connects. For Redis I had REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379 in .env, changed to 63790 — but still `ECONNREFUSED`. Logs from `docker-compose logs redis` show `Creating server TCP listening socket *:6379: Permission denied` earlier, but after I removed the host bindmount it started.

matt_b: Permission denied on bindmounts is common on mac. If the compose mounts `./redisdata:/data` and that dir is root-owned, Redis (running as non-root) can't bind. Two solutions: use a named volume (let Docker manage it) or chown the host dir to the uid used by the image. Example: `sudo chown -R 1000:1000 ./redisdata` (replace 1000 if different) then restart.

olivia_chen: I switched to a named volume for redis and that fixed the permission issue. Then remapped host port to 63790 and updated .env.local. Now both services start and the app connects.

ops-bot: Reminder: onboarding doc "local-services" has recommendations: prefer running app inside compose for parity, or use per-developer `.env.local` with remapped ports. https://redwood.example/docs/onboarding/local-services

sara_l: Also worth adding a small helper script we keep in repo: `scripts/dev-up.sh` that detects if brew services are running and warns, then brings compose up with a timestamped backup of host dirs if it needs to recreate them. Helps avoid surprises.

olivia_chen: That's awesome — I'll try `make dev` (mentioned in README) next. Thanks for the patient onboarding help, team! :wave: :tada:

matt_b: Welcome aboard — ping any of us if you want pairing to set up `.env.local` or the `dev-up.sh` script.
